content.intro: Learn database bulk-loading features through a short explanation, a concept diagram, and a PostgreSQL-oriented example. Focus on the reason for the query or design decision before memorizing syntax.
content.why_it_matters: Database Bulk-Loading Features matters because database behavior becomes more reliable when the intended row meaning, data shape, and edge cases are explicit. This lesson follows the SQL curriculum's listed subtopics and calls out PostgreSQL-specific behavior when it matters.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A safe database bulk-loading features workflow separates ingestion from trusted production tables. Load into staging, validate encodings and data quality, reconcile counts, then apply well-defined changes in a transaction or restartable batch.

items.title: Permissions and security restrictions
items.text: Permissions and security restrictions should be enforced at the database/application boundary rather than by UI checks alone. Bind data values as parameters, grant only the access a role needs, and test that unauthorized operations fail.

items.title: Transaction and error-handling behavior
items.text: Transaction and error-handling behavior is about keeping multi-step work correct when errors or other sessions intervene. Keep transactions short, define what must succeed together, handle conflicts explicitly, and test using separate sessions in a disposable database.

content_blocks.title: Remember
content_blocks.text: SQL correctness depends on data shape, constraints, NULL behavior, row counts, and the target database dialect—not just whether a statement parses.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a query is correct because it returns some rows.
common_mistakes.why: A result can omit valid records, multiply joined rows, mishandle NULLs, or rely on a non-deterministic order.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected row grain, add targeted edge cases, and use a stable tie-breaker whenever order or pagination matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying PostgreSQL syntax into another SQL engine without checking support.
common_mistakes.why: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, and Oracle differ in types, functions, row limits, procedural features, and transaction behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Label the target engine/version and verify the relevant official reference before adapting the query.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing with production data or credentials.
common_mistakes.why: Practice statements can change rows or expose sensitive information if run against the wrong connection.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a dedicated disposable lab, check current_database() and current_user, and review all changes before committing.
